name: Coverage check
summary: What the store holds: document count, actor count, date range, breakdown by source type and sub-pillar.
note: Counting and grouping only. No inference over content.
caveat: Tells you nothing about the world. A well-covered cell means we have read a lot, not that a field is crowded.

name: Adjacent actors
summary: A named list of actors adjacent to a candidate - same theme, same geography, related sub-pillar.
note: Buildable, not yet built. Needs no new field; deferred by choice.
caveat: Adjacency is judged on tags, not on knowledge of the field. A starting point for a conversation, not a shortlist of the right people.

name: Network position
summary: Actors bridging otherwise separate clusters - who connects the field.
caveat: The graph maps what we have read, not the field, and it skews to authors. Centrality must not be quoted until author-count weighting is applied.

name: Policy-implementation gap
summary: A commitment on the public record - a limit value, an NDC, a COP pledge - with no actor delivering it.
note: Highest-confidence candidate type: the demand side is stated, not inferred.
caveat: A commitment with no implementer in the store may still have implementers in the world. Public commitment removes the demand-side uncertainty, not the response-side one.

name: Scale mismatch
summary: A documented need and a documented response that differ by orders of magnitude.
note: The only candidate type that does not depend on absence.
caveat: The two numbers usually come from different sources with different scopes. Report the mismatch, never the multiple.

name: Proven but unscaled
summary: A solution that succeeded in one place and has not scaled.
note: Cannot be inferred reliably from free text - an agent cannot consistently tell 'piloted successfully in Kenya' from 'under development'.
caveat: Success is self-reported. A pilot described as successful in its own write-up may not have been.

name: Actor mix
summary: A field with researchers but no implementers, or implementers but no funders.
caveat: LEAD is filled largely by harvesting authors, and authors are overwhelmingly researchers. Every field will look research-heavy whether or not it is.

name: Venue shift
summary: A topic that has moved from research into regulator consultations or industry material.
missing_field: Source type field plus 12+ months of collection
note: The source type field exists in this build; the remaining blocker is elapsed collection time - the corpus was assembled, not accumulated.
caveat: Venue shift only works if you are reading all the venues. Without even coverage across source types this measures reading habits rather than the world.

name: Transferability
summary: A case study whose enabling conditions also appear elsewhere - worked in A, might work in B.
missing_field: Enabling conditions list per case study
note: Not one column - a structured list.
caveat: Most transfer failures happen because a condition nobody wrote down was doing the work. The only analysis here where being wrong costs money directly rather than costing attention.

name: Sub-pillar co-occurrence
summary: Two well-covered sub-pillars that rarely appear together.
note: Buildable, not yet built. Needs no new field; deferred by choice.
caveat: Most non-co-occurrences are simply unrelated things. Any two topics can be made to sound like a promising intersection after the fact.

name: Problem rising, response static
summary: Evidence about a problem growing year on year while actor count stays flat.
caveat: The corpus was assembled, not accumulated. An apparent rise may simply be recent reading. Treat any trend line as a description of collection activity.

name: Gap analysis
summary: A documented problem with few actors working on it. Produces the six-section LION output.
note: Lowest-trust candidate type in the catalogue. Implemented first only because it is the only one the current fields support.
caveat: The output most likely to be a coverage artefact and the one people find most convincing. Never present it without the coverage figure from #1 alongside it.

name: Well resourced, not working
summary: A field with actors, funding and attention that is not producing results.
caveat: Reporting is systematically positive. A field can look like it is working while producing nothing, and the stores will never show the difference.

name: Fund flows
summary: Direction and rate of change of funding into a theme.
note: A budget conversation, not a build one. Historical deal data must be bought or accumulated over years.
caveat: Rate-of-change analysis on incomplete data mostly measures changes in disclosure practice. The failure mode that looks most like a finding.

name: Failure mapping
summary: A record of what has been attempted and failed.
note: The only thing that distinguishes 'nobody tried' from 'someone tried and failed'. Every other analysis sees identical silence in both cases.
caveat: What gets recorded as failure is a fraction of what failed. Absence of a recorded failure is not evidence that nothing was tried.

name: Crowded field
summary: A theme with many actors, or many capital providers, already present.
caveat: LEAD is not a funder database. Funders rarely author documents. Reading 'no funders present' as 'no funders active' would be a serious error.
